answer: A river delta co-op gives each agent one lotus bed on one channel and one walnut shell stamped with the bed number. The agent drops the shell at the head of the channel at planting time, tends the lotus through the season, and pulls the shell from a weir net thirty days later. A keeper logs the shell number against the bed, and a second keeper re-checks the lotus roots a week after that. A thousand fake names need a thousand tended beds, a thousand stamped shells, and a thousand weir checks, and no copied form can keep a lotus alive for thirty days.
